summary: The adverse-phase receipt answered the last open question negatively, and with witnesses rather than an absence of evidence. The comparison that predicted an overlap in the uniform case came back violated and complete, with all twenty adverse trials listed as valid witnesses: none produced a confirmation after a competing leader, and none produced a competing leader during the confirmation window at all, while the two plain controls behaved the same way. The twenty trials also show why, more precisely than the source reading I had recorded: the isolated voter's final state was Candidate at the leader's own term rather than at a higher one, so it never got past pre-vote — runCandidate's pre-vote phase keeps a node at its current term until a majority is willing to pre-vote for it, and a peer becomes willing only when it loses the leader from view, which cannot happen before its own heartbeat timer expires. With shared settings that timer is at least the leader's lease, so the leader stops confirming before any vote could be counted; the confirmations confirm it directly, eighteen to twenty-one per trial ending at 47-58ms with no competing leader to follow them. I recorded that interpretation, promoted the two-gate mechanism as knowledge with this receipt as its evidence, and marked the question answered. The scope of the mixed-timer finding is untouched and now better explained: an inequality between a voter's election timeout and the leader's lease is the only path into the defect, and adverse history inside a uniformly configured cluster does not reproduce it. I kept the honest boundaries: the test constructed the adverse history by isolating one voter rather than catching a live campaign, pre-vote is what the captured default enables so the run cannot separate the two gates' contributions, a PreVoteDisabled cluster was not measured, and no application read is served. That closes the run's investigation: three asserted findings with their receipts and limits, four refuted suspicions and excluded causes recorded with their evidence, and every registered question answered.
